- `scms_core/linkage.py` (whole file) CAMP SCP2: seed hash-chain ls_x(i)=trunc128(SHA256(la_id||ls||0^112)) (:71-77), Davies-Meyer AES pre-linkage trunc-72 (:90-97), lv=plv1 XOR plv2 (:100-104), forward-only `CrlLinkageEntry.matches` (:156-172). Wired into the dataset path (run.py:2110, 2700-2701) and ASSERTED at run.py:3655-3658 ("CRL entry failed to revoke a pseudonym of its target device"). Java mirror `org/scms/crypto/LinkageEngine.java`, consistency checked at ScmsBackend.java:855-857.
- `scms_core/butterfly.py` CAMP SCP1 butterfly expansion: f1/f2 AES-128 (:54-61), RA cocoon B=A+f1*G, Q=P+f2*G (:96-100), PCA explicit certify (:103-110), device re-derivation b_i+c (:113-115). Correct, but ORPHANED — run.py imports only crypto_abstract and linkage (run.py:44-45); exercised only by tests/test_butterfly.py.

coupling:
HARD-WIRED, non-standard, and blocking:
- ONE message construction site, one bespoke shape: run.py:3186-3189 `b_cam = dict(veh, digest, cx, cy, cs, ch, conf, ghost, x, y, falsified, msg_count, cg, sig_ok, cvf, cvt, station_type, tspd, thdg)`. There is no message class, no container model, no codec. Java equivalent SignedCam.java:16-49 (12 fields). No ASN.1/OER/UPER/COER encoder anywhere (grep asn1|uper|oer|psid|itsAid over src/ and scms-sim/: zero hits) -> nothing is byte-encodable, so no interoperability claim is testable.
- CAM emission is a FIXED per-step loop, not a triggering rule: run.py:3092 `for step in range(n_steps)`, :3099 `t = step*cfg.dt`, :3114 `for tx in active_list:` -> exactly one broadcast per active vehicle per step; `dt: float = 1.0` (run.py:720) -> a rigid 1 Hz. The 4 m/4 deg/0.5 m/s thresholds are pinned in refdata but have NO consumer in Python (verified by grep). realism_bench.py:1881-1883 admits it in the metric note.
- Units/frames are engine-private and mutually incompatible: Python heading = deg CCW from East, position = local metres, speed = float m/s, gen time = float seconds (declared at run.py:3789-3793 `conventions`). ETSI requires 0.1 deg CW from North, WGS84 1/10 microdegree, 0.01 m/s, generationDeltaTime = ms mod 65536 since 2004 TAI. Java/SUMO uses a THIRD convention (deg CW from North). Any standards profile must therefore also be a unit-conversion plugin.
- Position confidence is a single scalar circular radius `conf = 2.448*sqrt(sigma_nom^2 + bias_x^2 + bias_y^2)` (run.py:2427), not ETSI's PosConfidenceEllipse{semiMajorConfidence, semiMinorConfidence, semiMajorOrientation}. `posConf` in Java is likewise one double (SignedCam.java:29).
- `station_type` is a two-valued string "vehicle"|"vru" (run.py:3169-3171) gated on an opt-in flag (`_emit_station_type`, run.py:1971), not the ETSI StationType enum 0..15. The real fleet classes car/motorcycle/truck/bus (run.py:142-147) are ORACLE-only and never reach the wire.
- NO SIGNING HAPPENS. run.py imports crypto_abstract as `ca` (:44) and calls only keypair_from_seed / public_bytes / hashed_id8 / canonical_bytes — grep for `ca.sign(` / `ca.verify(` in run.py: ZERO hits. Signature validity is a boolean `sig_ok` set by the attack switch (run.py:3142, 3156-3157) and read as a flag (run.py:3395). The Java layer has no crypto at all: `send(...)` passes literal `true` for sigValid (ScmsBeaconApp.java:294); cert digests are `hex(sha("cert|"+MASTER_SEED+"|"+unitId),8)` (ScmsBackend.java:312) — a hash of a STRING, not of a public key; grep ECDSA|secp256|Signature over the Java tree: zero.
- Certificate = a hex string plus {i, j, lv, valid_from, valid_to, issuing_pca:"PCA-1"} (run.py:2109-2111, 3668-3672; records.MaCertStatus :117-131). No ToBeSignedCertificate, issuer, cracaId, crlSeries, region, assuranceLevel, appPermissions/PsidSsp, verifyKeyIndicator, certificate signature. The linkage value is real but lives in a side dict `pseudonym_info` (run.py:2110), not inside a certificate structure.
- Pseudonym provisioning bypasses butterfly entirely: run.py:2098-2100 `i_k, j_k = k // jmax, (vid+k) % jmax` and `pk = ca.keypair_from_seed(cfg.derive(f"key:{vid}:{k}"))` — every pseudonym of a device derives from one label, the exact OPPOSITE of the unlinkability butterfly.py implements. No provisioning request/response, no encryption to the PCA, no RA shuffling, no batch/topping-off.
- Revocation publishes ls_x(0), not ls_x(i): run.py:2697-2701 (`la1.seed_at(handle, 0)` ... "revoke from period 0 -> covers ALL"). This DESTROYS the backward-privacy property that linkage.py:16-19 documents and that CrlLinkageEntry.matches (:162-163) exists to enforce — the published CRL entry links the device's entire history, not only from period i forward. Same in Java, except Java correctly uses `p.i` (ScmsBackend.java:851-852) — the two engines diverge on this security property.
- TS 103 759 reported-message container is MISSING: `evidence_msg_refs=[f"{rid}-m"]` (run.py:2620) is a self-referential synthetic id pointing at nothing; the written file set (run.py:3732-3741, 3752-3758) contains no evidence table. `MaEvidenceMessage` (records.py:76-92) is NEVER INSTANTIATED by the pipeline — grep shows only records.py and tests/test_leakage.py:13,68.
- `cert_validity` is a hard-coded constant `{"sig_valid":True,"not_expired":True,"not_revoked":True,"chain_ok":True}` on EVERY report (run.py:2619), as are `row["cert_crl_status"]="active"` (:2626). This is written even for reports about an ExpiredCert / NotYetValid / InvalidSignature subject — a factual defect, not merely a standards gap.
- Detector suites are two independent hard-coded lists with inline scoring: Python DET_KEYS tuple (run.py:2570-2584) + inline blocks (run.py:3409-3531); Java CamDetector.java with env-var thresholds (:26-41). No registration point, no interface.
- Reason codes are F2MD detector names ("positionSpeedInconsistency", "acceptanceRangeThreshold", "sybilCoLocation", ...) not TS 103 759 SemanticDetection* enumerations.
- Frame size is a magic 300 B in both engines (SignedCam.java:18, Dcc.java:81 default) — ignores TS 103 097 certificate-attachment alternation (full cert ~350-500 B vs digest signer ~200-300 B), so the CBR estimate is systematically wrong.
- No standards test exists: 57 files in tests/, none asserts a standards property.

determinism_risks: Any new emitted field or record moves data_digest. The repo's existing discipline is to gate EVERY addition behind an opt-in flag (`_emit_station_type` run.py:1971, `_denm_enabled` run.py:1983, DET_KEYS gating run.py:2578-2584, subclassed rows `_MaCertStatusVru`/`_GtVehicleVru`). A standards-profile plugin MUST default to `native_v1` and be a config field, or every pinned golden digest breaks on the first standards-compliant CAM.

ETSI CAM triggering in the Python engine is NOT a gated addition — it changes the NUMBER of broadcasts per step, hence the number of receptions, hence every subsequent draw from the single order-sensitive global stream `rng = random.Random(cfg.seed)` (consumed at run.py:2611 report ingest delay, :3230 emission sampling, :3384 packet loss, plus the report_prob coins). One extra/missing broadcast invalidates all downstream output. Same for any detector plugin that changes which reports are filed -> which vehicles are revoked -> which vehicles are `enforced()` -> the broadcast set.

DCC in the Python engine is a FEEDBACK loop (emissions -> CBR -> permitted rate -> emissions). Digest stability would then depend on the exact accumulation and iteration order of the CBR estimator, which is far more fragile than the current one-way per-step loop. Java sidesteps this by having per-station Dcc instances with drift-free probe boundaries (Dcc.java:128-150) — a Python port must replicate that boundary computation exactly or the two engines diverge non-reproducibly.

Swapping crypto_abstract to ECDSA P-256 to satisfy IEEE 1609.2 breaks byte-identical output: ECDSA is randomised unless RFC 6979 deterministic-k is mandated. The current choice of Ed25519 is deliberate and documented for exactly this reason (crypto_abstract.py:5-8). A signature plugin contract must REQUIRE deterministic nonces, and the manifest must record which.

A third-party detector plugin can trivially destroy determinism: drawing from the global `rng`, using module-level `random`, iterating a `set`, reading the wall clock, or using unseeded numpy. The established convention is one dedicated string-keyed stream per feature (`random.Random(f"{cfg.seed}:<label>:{id}")`, e.g. run.py:2055, 2181, 2335, 3352-3353). The plugin API must HAND the plugin its own derived stream and make the global stream unreachable.

Plugin discovery order is an environment variable in disguise. setuptools entry_points / directory scanning is install-order and filesystem-order dependent. Discovery must be an explicit ORDERED list in the config, and the resolved load order + each plugin's name, version, config hash and source hash must land in manifest.json, or the replay contract (`--config manifest.json`) silently reproduces a different run.

Leakage-linter bypass. records.is_forbidden_feature_key (records.py:52-70) is prefix/suffix/exact-match based. A plugin free to name its own output columns can surface ground truth under a name the pattern misses — the code already flags this exact hazard for `is_vru` vs `is_vru_declared` (records.py:40-42). A plugin's declared outputs must be whitelisted against a schema, not merely pattern-checked, and a plugin must be denied access to any ORACLE-side object (today `b_cam` carries `x`, `y`, `tspd`, `thdg`, `falsified` in the SAME dict a detector could be handed — run.py:3186-3189).

Two-engine divergence is already a live determinism/semantics bug, not a hypothetical: revocation period (run.py:2697-2698 uses i=0 vs ScmsBackend.java:851-852 uses p.i), heading convention (CCW-from-East vs CW-from-North), CAM triggering (absent vs present). Adding plugins without a single shared spec multiplies this. Any standards plugin needs a cross-engine conformance test — none of the 57 test files currently asserts a standards property.

Windows / no-shapely / no-scipy constraint bites the codec plugin: asn1tools and pycrate pull compiled or heavyweight deps. A pure-Python OER/UPER encoder is feasible but must be byte-stable across Python versions (dict ordering, float repr) — the repo's existing answer is `ca.canonical_bytes` (crypto_abstract.py:28-40, sorted keys, separators, ensure_ascii, bytes->hex), which is the right precedent but does NOT give ASN.1 OER.
notes:
PER-STANDARD VERDICTS (evidence-first; no compliance credited that is not in the code).

=== 1. ETSI EN 302 637-2 V1.4.1 "ITS; Vehicular Communications; Basic Set of Applications; Part 2: Specification of Cooperative Awareness Basic Service" ===
REQUIRES: ItsPduHeader{protocolVersion, messageID=2, stationID} + CoopAwareness{generationDeltaTime, camParameters{basicContainer{stationType(0..15), referencePosition{latitude, longitude (1/10 microdeg), positionConfidenceEllipse{semiMajorConfidence, semiMinorConfidence, semiMajorOrientation}, altitude}}, highFrequencyContainer(BasicVehicleContainerHighFrequency: heading+headingConfidence, speed+speedConfidence, driveDirection, vehicleLength, vehicleWidth, longitudinalAcceleration, curvature, curvatureCalculationMode, yawRate, + optional accelerationControl, lanePosition, steeringWheelAngle, lateral/vertical accel, performanceClass, cenDsrcTollingZone), lowFrequencyContainer(vehicleRole, exteriorLights, pathHistory) at least every 500 ms, specialVehicleContainer}}. Generation rules: T_GenCamMin=100 ms, T_GenCamMax=1000 ms, T_CheckGenCam; trigger on |dPos|>4 m OR |dHeading|>4 deg OR |dSpeed|>0.5 m/s; after a dynamics trigger, emit N_GenCam(=3) consecutive CAMs at that interval before relaxing to T_GenCamMax; T_GenCam constrained by DCC.
REPO — Python flagship: NO CAM object, NO containers, NO ItsPduHeader. The broadcast is run.py:3186-3189, a dict of 19 keys of which the wire-visible ones are cx, cy, cs, ch, conf, cg, sig_ok, cvf, cvt, station_type — roughly 8 of ~40 mandatory HF-container fields, in the wrong units and the wrong frame. Emission is a fixed per-step loop (run.py:3092/3099/3114) at dt=1.0 (run.py:720) -> rigid 1 Hz, i.e. permanently pinned at T_GenCamMax with the dynamics trigger, N_GenCam and T_CheckGenCam all absent. The 4 m / 4 deg / 0.5 m/s constants are pinned in refdata/etsi_cam_dcc.json:cam_trigger_thresholds and explicitly annotated "PINNED FOR PHASE 2" — no Python consumer exists. realism_bench.py:1881-1883 states this in the metric note itself.
REPO — MOSAIC/Java: ScmsBeaconApp.java:229-233 implements the dynamics trigger + T_GenCamMin floor + T_GenCamMax heartbeat correctly; missing N_GenCam repeats and an explicit T_CheckGenCam (approximated by the 0.1 s vehicle-update cadence). Field set is SignedCam.java:20-31 — same poverty as Python.
VERDICT: message STRUCTURE = ABSENT (both engines). Generation RULES = PARTIAL (Java only, ScmsBeaconApp.java:229-233), ABSENT in the Python dataset flagship.

=== 2. ETSI EN 302 637-3 "…Part 3: Specification of Decentralized Environmental Notification Basic Service" ===
REQUIRES: ItsPduHeader{messageID=1} + DENM{management{actionID{originatingStationID, sequenceNumber}, detectionTime, referenceTime, termination(isCancellation|isNegation), eventPosition, relevanceDistance, relevanceTrafficDirection, validityDuration (default 600 s), transmissionInterval, stationType}, situation{informationQuality, eventType{causeCode, subCauseCode}, linkedCause, eventHistory}, location{eventSpeed, eventPositionHeading, traces, roadType}, alacarte}; lifecycle new/update/cancellation/negation, repetition at transmissionInterval for repetitionDuration, T_O_Validity expiry, keep-alive forwarding.
REPO (opt-in, default OFF — run.py:1983): emit_denm run.py:2661-2690. Broadcast keys add only `msg_type="denm"`, `event_type`, `denm_id`. MA-visible row (run.py:2680-2683) = {denm_id, cert_digest, detection_time, event_type, claimed_x, claimed_y, claimed_speed, denm_plausibility}. event_type is one of two ETSI cause-code NAMES only — "emergencyElectronicBrakeLight" (CauseCode 99) and "stationaryVehicle" (94) at run.py:3202/3212-3213 — with no numeric causeCode/subCauseCode. eventPosition is not distinct from the sender's claimed CAM position (run.py:2671). ABSENT: actionID, referenceTime, termination/cancellation/negation, validityDuration, transmissionInterval, REPETITION (each DENM is appended exactly once, run.py:2675), relevanceDistance, relevanceTrafficDirection, traces, roadType, informationQuality, linkedCause, alacarte. No DENM in the Java layer at all.
VERDICT: ABSENT. The specific mechanisms asked about — termination and repetition — do not exist in any form.

=== 3. ETSI TS 103 300-3 "ITS; Vulnerable Road Users (VRU) awareness; Part 3: Specification of VRU awareness basic service" (VAM) ===
REQUIRES: messageID=16 VruAwareness{generationDeltaTime, vamParameters{basicContainer{stationType (pedestrian 1/cyclist 2/moped 3/motorcycle 4/animal 11), referencePosition}, vruHighFrequencyContainer{heading, speed, longitudinalAcceleration, + optional curvature, yawRate, lateral/vertical accel, vruLanePosition, environment, movementControl, orientation, rollAngle, deviceUsage}, vruLowFrequencyContainer{profileAndSubprofile, exteriorLights, sizeClass}, vruClusterInformation{clusterId, boundingBox, cardinality}, vruClusterOperationContainer{join/leave/breakUp/idChange}, vruMotionPredictionContainer{pathHistory, pathPrediction, safeDistance, trajectoryInterception}}}; T_GenVamMin 100 ms / T_GenVamMax 5000 ms, 4 m / 4 deg / 0.5 m/s triggers plus cluster-state triggers and redundancy mitigation.
REPO: NO VAM exists. VRUs (opt-in vru_pct, run.py:847; make_vru run.py:2173+) emit the SAME CAM dict with `station_type="vru"` (run.py:3169). No VruProfile, no cluster containers, no motion prediction, no redundancy mitigation, no T_GenVam. The only VRU-specific behaviour is receiver-side detector exemption (run.py:3485-3500) and a plausibility bound VRU_MAX_PLAUSIBLE_SPEED_MPS=10.0 (run.py:136). VRUs are excluded from the receiver set (run.py:3263). Zero VRU/pedestrian code in the entire MOSAIC/Java tree (verified by grep).
VERDICT: ABSENT. The comments "they broadcast VAMs" (run.py:3259) and "VAM-broadcasting devices" (run.py:841) are aspirational and should be corrected — nothing VAM-shaped is emitted.

=== 4. SAE J2735 (Basic Safety Message) and SAE J2945/1 (On-Board System Requirements for V2V Safety Communications) ===
J2735 BSM REQUIRES Part I: msgCnt, id (4-octet TemporaryID), secMark, lat/long/elev, positionalAccuracy{semiMajor, semiMinor, orientation}, transmissionState, speed, heading, angle, accelSet{long, lat, vert, yaw}, brakes{wheelBrakes, traction, abs, scs, brakeBoost, auxBrakes}, size{width, length}; Part II VehicleSafetyExtensions{events, pathHistory, pathPrediction, exteriorLights}. J2945/1 REQUIRES 10 Hz nominal rate, congestion control on channel busy, PathHistory with 300 m span / 1 m allowable error, PathPrediction radius of curvature, position/speed/heading accuracy minimums, and 1609.2 signing with full-certificate attachment at least every 450 ms (digest otherwise).
REPO: nothing. Two comments only: SignedCam.java:18 `// signed CAM ~ headers + BSM/CAM + 1609.2 sig` and records.py:78 `"A signed CAM/BSM enclosed as report evidence"`. No BSM record, no TemporaryID, no msgCnt, no BrakeSystemStatus, no PathHistory/PathPrediction, no 10 Hz rate, no certificate-attachment policy.
VERDICT: ABSENT. Note the architectural inconsistency: the project's PKI model is deliberately US-side (ADR 0001:26-27) while its message model is nominally ETSI-side — the pairing (US SCMS + CAM/DENM) exists in no real deployment.

=== 5. ETSI TS 103 097 (Security header and certificate formats) + IEEE 1609.2 (Security Services for Applications and Management Messages) ===
IEEE 1609.2 REQUIRES: Ieee1609Dot2Data{protocolVersion=3, content=signedData{hashId, tbsData=ToBeSignedData{payload{data|extDataHash}, headerInfo{psid (mandatory), generationTime, expiryTime, generationLocation, p2pcdLearningRequest, missingCrlIdentifier, ...}}, signer=SignerIdentifier{digest HashedId8 | certificate SequenceOfCertificate | self}, signature=EcdsaP256Signature{rSig, sSig}}}; certificates = CertificateBase{version=3, type(explicit|implicit), issuer{sha256AndDigest|self}, toBeSigned=ToBeSignedCertificate{id{linkageData{iCert, linkage-value, group-linkage-value}|name|binaryId|none}, cracaId, crlSeries, validityPeriod{start, duration}, region, assuranceLevel, appPermissions SequenceOfPsidSsp, certIssuePermissions, verifyKeyIndicator{verificationKey|reconstructionValue}}, signature}. TS 103 097 profiles this: psid mandatory, generationTime mandatory for CAM/DENM, chain-length limits, signer alternation (full certificate at least every 1 s for CAMs), permitted curves NIST P-256 / brainpoolP256r1 / brainpoolP384r1, SSP formats.
REPO: `crypto_abstract.hashed_id8` (:58-60) is the only genuine 1609.2 element. sign/verify exist (:63-74) and are NEVER CALLED from run.py (verified by grep) — signature validity is the boolean `sig_ok` (run.py:3142, 3156-3157, 3395). The Java layer contains no cryptography whatsoever: literal `true` at ScmsBeaconApp.java:294; cert digest = SHA-256 of a string, not of a key (ScmsBackend.java:312). No SignedData, no tbsData, no headerInfo, no psid/ITS-AID, no generationTime-in-header, no signer alternation, no EcdsaP256Signature, no certificate structure of any kind (the cert is a hex string + validity window + `issuing_pca="PCA-1"`, run.py:3668-3672). ec.py (real secp256r1) and butterfly.py are correct but disconnected from the dataset path. No ASN.1/OER encoder anywhere.
VERDICT: IEEE 1609.2 = ABSENT except HashedId8. TS 103 097 = ABSENT (zero profile constraints implemented). The manifest claim `"cert": "IEEE 1609.2"` (run.py:3794, ScmsBackend.java:1029) and DATASHEET.md:33 ("certificates profiled to IEEE 1609.2") are NOT supported by the code and should be downgraded to "HashedId8 identifiers per IEEE 1609.2" or similar.

=== 6. ETSI TS 102 941 (Trust and Privacy Management) vs the US SCMS ===
TS 102 941 REQUIRES: EnrolmentRequest/Response (InnerEcRequest{itsId, certificateFormat, publicKeys, requestedSubjectAttributes}, self-signed with the canonical key, encrypted to the EA), AuthorizationRequest/Response (InnerAtRequest{publicKeys, hmacKey, sharedAtRequest, ecSignature}, double-envelope so the AA cannot link to the EC and the EA cannot learn the AT key), AuthorizationValidationRequest/Response (AA<->EA), CA Certificate Request, CTL/ECTL distribution (TLM/CPOC), CRL, and (from v1.4.1) butterfly-key AT provisioning; all carried in EtsiTs103097Data-Signed/-Encrypted.
REPO models the US SCMS by explicit decision (docs/adr/0001-stack-and-approach.md:26-27, which also promises "ETSI TS 102 941 kept as a config variant" — no such config field exists anywhere).
US SCMS fidelity — WHAT IS REAL: linkage values SCP2 fully and correctly implemented AND enforced (linkage.py; run.py:2110/2700-2701; assertion run.py:3655-3658; Java LinkageEngine + self-check ScmsBackend.java:855-857). Butterfly SCP1 correctly implemented (butterfly.py:54-120) against Brecht et al. arXiv:1802.05323 but ORPHANED. Entity trust boundaries are structural (run.py:976-1021; Scms.java:31-53, 14 entities incl. Electors 3/quorum 2, PolicyGenerator jmax=20 iPeriod=10080 min, LocationObscurerProxy).
US SCMS fidelity — WHAT IS NOT: no provisioning protocol at all (no request/response, no encryption to the PCA, no RA shuffling, no batch or topping-off); pseudonyms are n_rot Ed25519 keys derived from `cfg.derive(f"key:{vid}:{k}")` (run.py:2099) — all of a device's pseudonyms derivable from one label, the opposite of butterfly unlinkability; i/j assigned arithmetically (run.py:2098) rather than by certificate batch; ECA issues `sha16("enroll|"+unitId)` with no enrolment protocol (Scms.java:130-132); Electors/PolicyGenerator/DCM are constant stubs (Scms.java:93-119); no CRACA, no crlSeries, no CRL signing, no CRL wire format, no distribution schedule. SECURITY DEFECT: the Python engine revokes from period 0 (run.py:2697-2698), publishing ls_x(0) and thereby linking the device's ENTIRE history — destroying the forward-only/backward-privacy property that linkage.py:16-19 documents and CrlLinkageEntry.matches:162-163 enforces. Java does it correctly with p.i (ScmsBackend.java:851-852). The two engines therefore disagree on a core privacy property.
ETSI divergence, none of it modelled: no EA/AA roles, no EC/AT distinction (there is no enrolment credential in the Python engine — RA.bind maps request_hash->true_vehicle_id directly, run.py:1015-1016), no AuthorizationValidation, no ECTL/CTL/TLM/CPOC, no EtsiTs103097Data envelopes, no certificateFormat, no ITS-AID/PSID SSP.
VERDICT: US SCMS = PARTIAL, and the strongest standards work in the project (linkage layer is genuinely compliant and enforced). ETSI TS 102 941 = ABSENT.

=== 7. ETSI TS 103 759 "ITS; Security; Misbehaviour Reporting Service; Release 2" ===
REQUIRES: MisbehaviorReport carried as EtsiTs103097Data-Signed (and encrypted to the MA), containing {version, generationTime, reportMetadataContainer{reportID, generationTime, relatedReportContainer{relatedReportID, omittedReportsNumber}, reportedStationType}, reportContainer{reportedMessageContainer — the ACTUAL secured PDUs of the reported station, evidenceContainer{neighbourMessageContainer (the reporter's own observed CAMs/DENMs), senderInfoContainer (reporter state at detection), certificateContainer (certs needed to verify)}, misbehaviourTypeContainer{semanticDetectionReferenceCAM / semanticDetectionRelativeCAM / semanticDetectionReferenceDENM / ... with NORMATIVE detection-reason enumerations}}}.
REPO: records.MaReport (records.py:94-115) produced at run.py:2613-2643, Java at ScmsBackend.java:800-811. Fields: report_id, ingest_time, detection_time, generation_time, reporter_cert_digest, subject_cert_digest, reason_codes[], detector_outputs[{check_id, score, verdict}], cert_validity{...}, evidence_msg_refs[], st_bbox[4], st_tstart, st_tend, duplicate_flag, + detector_score, detector_score_norm, subject_pos_confidence, cert_crl_status, sig_valid, optional station_type/rssi_dbm, and ~13 detnorm_* columns.
CORRESPONDENCE THAT IS REAL: a report identifier; generation and detection times; reporter and subject identified ONLY by certificate digest (HashedId8-shaped, no identity — the leakage firewall at records.py:33-70 is a stronger privacy discipline than F2MD's, and is enforced by datagen/leakage_linter.py); a detection-reason list; an evidence reference list; and MA-side unlinkability via the LocationObscurerProxy (Scms.java:259-262).
CORRESPONDENCE THAT IS NOT: (a) the reportedMessageContainer — the MANDATORY CORE of the standard — does not exist. `evidence_msg_refs=[f"{rid}-m"]` (run.py:2620) is a synthetic self-reference; no evidence table is in the written file set (run.py:3732-3741, 3752-3758); `MaEvidenceMessage` (records.py:76-92) is never instantiated by the pipeline (only records.py + tests/test_leakage.py:13,68). Every filed report is therefore unverifiable by construction — an MA could not re-check a single claim. (b) no neighbourMessageContainer, senderInfoContainer, certificateContainer, relatedReportContainer/omittedReportsNumber, reportedStationType, or version. (c) reason_codes are F2MD detector names, not the normative SemanticDetection* enumerations. (d) `cert_validity` is a hard-coded all-True constant on every report (run.py:2619), as is `cert_crl_status="active"` (run.py:2626) — written even for ExpiredCert / NotYetValid / InvalidSignature subjects; this is a defect independent of standards. (e) st_bbox / st_tstart / st_tend / detnorm_* are ML feature columns with no TS 103 759 counterpart. (f) reports are neither signed nor encrypted nor ASN.1-encoded.
VERDICT: PARTIAL at the level of field NAMES only. The manifest's own wording `"report": "ETSI TS 103 759 (shape)"` (run.py:3794) is the honest statement; DATASHEET.md:34 and records.py:96 ("shaped to TS 103 759") overstate it. Given the project's stated purpose is misbehaviour-detection datasets, the missing reportedMessageContainer is the single most consequential compliance gap in the repo and the highest-value thing to fix — and the record class for it already exists, unused.

=== 8. ETSI TS 102 687 V1.2.1 "Decentralized Congestion Control Mechanisms for ITS operating in the 5 GHz range" ===
REQUIRES: access-layer DCC; CBR = fraction of 100 ms-window probes measuring above -85 dBm; reactive state machine Relaxed/Active1-3/Restrictive mapping CBR to T_off (10/5/2.5/2/1 Hz at 0.30/0.40/0.50/0.60); or adaptive LIMERIC-derived delta control (alpha=0.016, beta=0.0012, CBR_target=0.68, delta_max=0.03, 200 ms update); NDL_minDccSampling ~1 s state hold; transmit power control; per-traffic-class queueing.
REPO — Java: Dcc.java is a genuine and careful reactive implementation (exact step table :48-49; correct 802.11p 10 MHz airtime :99-104; 100 ms probes over a ~1 s window with drift-free boundaries :128-150; state hold :189-199; suppression counters to the manifest). Correctly noted at ScmsBeaconApp.java:217-224 that DCC never stretches past T_GenCamMax. OPT-IN, default OFF (SCMS_DCC=1). Gaps even here, self-declared at Dcc.java:18-35: CBR is frames-sensed x airtime / window, NOT an energy probe against -85 dBm; no adaptive/LIMERIC variant; no TPC; no per-class queueing; no cross-layer TS 103 175 management entity; DCC gates CAM emission only.
REPO — Python flagship: NO DCC. `PHY_CS_THRESHOLD_DBM = -85.0` (run.py:306) is used only for a sensing-range budget (run.py:577); the CBR at run.py:586-600 exists only inside the opt-in geometric channel and feeds hidden-terminal collision loss (run.py:3376), never the message rate. `chan_capacity=40` (run.py:787) is an ad-hoc congestion-loss knob, not DCC.
VERDICT: PARTIAL in the MOSAIC layer (reactive only, opt-in); ABSENT in the Python dataset flagship.

=== CROSS-CUTTING ===
- Root cause of nearly every gap: the project models the OUTCOMES of standardised operations (signature valid/invalid, cert expired/revoked, hazard real/fake) rather than the standardised STRUCTURES that carry them. This is a defensible research choice and crypto_abstract.py:1-13 states it explicitly — but it means "standards-compliant" cannot currently be claimed for anything except CAMP SCP2 linkage values.
- No test in the 57-file suite asserts a standards property. A conformance-test seam is a prerequisite for any standards-compliance work.
- Recommended documentation correction regardless of any code change: DATASHEET.md:32-34, README.md:133, docs/FEATURES.md:207, records.py:96 and the manifest `standards_profile` should distinguish IMPLEMENTED (CAMP SCP2 linkage; IEEE 1609.2 HashedId8; EN 302 637-2 triggering in the MOSAIC layer; TS 102 687 reactive DCC in the MOSAIC layer, opt-in) from INSPIRED-BY (report field names, DENM cause-code names, station types) from ABSENT (all message encodings, all security envelopes, all certificate structures, VAM, BSM, TS 102 941).
